title: Define administrative analytics contract
acceptance_criteria: Admin-only endpoints for users, role changes, analytics, audit logs, and cost metrics are enumerated

resolution: Source-verified complete (batch 2). Auth-domain admin endpoints enumerated: GET /api/v1/auth/admin/users (list users), POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-role (role change with BE token-version revocation), POST /api/v1/auth/admin/reset-password (generate reset token). Role-sensitive assumptions documented: role source of truth is authUser.role from /auth/me; FE enforces role gating at view-routing layer (handleChangeView) and render layer (activeView === VIEW_ADMIN && authUser.role === 'admin'); self-demotion guard redirects to VIEW_CHAT; bootstrap hydration loads admin data only for admin users. Operational telemetry explicitly separated from end-user knowledge features: different endpoint prefixes (/knowledge/admin/* vs /knowledge/documents/*), different state slots (adminAnalytics/adminAuditLogs/adminCostMetrics vs knowledgeDocuments/knowledgeChunks/knowledgeJobs), different presentation components (AdminPanel vs KnowledgePanel), different access control (admin-only vs any authenticated user). See Admin Analytics Contract Delta in docs/plan.md.

title: Document deployment and runtime configuration dependencies
acceptance_criteria: Deployment artifacts and environment variables are cataloged
Static frontend hosting and backend API dependency are documented together
Build-time versus runtime configuration constraints are identified
resolution: Source-verified complete (batch 2). Dockerfile: two-stage build (node:20-alpine build stage + nginx:1.27-alpine serve stage); VITE_API_BASE_URL and VITE_API_TIMEOUT_MS accepted as Docker ARG (defaults: https://api.dominicapp.dev and 120000); ARG promoted to ENV before npm run build so Vite bakes them into the bundle; static dist copied to /usr/share/nginx/html; port 80 exposed; health check at GET /healthz. nginx.conf: /healthz returns 200 ok (no access log); /assets/ served with 30-day Cache-Control public immutable; / uses try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html for SPA routing; no backend proxy configured. .env.example: VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000, VITE_API_TIMEOUT_MS=120000; documents same-host empty-URL mode but this mode is NOT supported by current resolveBaseUrl() — explicit URL required. .env.production: VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://api.dominicapp.dev, VITE_API_TIMEOUT_MS=120000. Build-time vs runtime: all VITE_* values are baked at build time by Vite static replacement; runtime reconfiguration without rebuild is not supported. Static hosting: frontend is a static SPA with hard dependency on backend at VITE_API_BASE_URL; no offline mode, no service worker; localStorage keys dominic.authToken and dominic.refreshToken persist across sessions. CORS required between frontend and backend in all deployment modes. See OPS-001 Deployment and Runtime Configuration Delta in docs/plan.md.

title: Source-verify SSE event contract for /api/v1/chat/stream
decision_note: CHAT-BE-002 is complete. Canonical SSE completion policy is success => final and failure => error. final is not guaranteed on failure paths, and no backend implementation task is required for the decision itself.
substeps: CHAT-BE-002-VERIFY: DONE — stream_message() at chat.py:249 emits error SSE events with status_code+detail for all exception types via _sse_event(); test_stream_internal_errors_are_sanitized passes. Error event shape confirmed against consumeSseStream() expectations.

CHAT-BE-002-DECIDE: DONE — canonical stream completion policy is success => final and failure => error. Option 2 (always emit final on failure) is rejected because it blurs terminal semantics, expands FE/BE test scope, and still cannot cover pre-handshake HTTP failures. FE must treat error as terminal rather than waiting for final.
acceptance_criteria: SSE event types start, delta, error, and final are confirmed present or absent in backend source
Whether stream completion without a final event is possible is documented
How error events are encoded (detail, status_code) is confirmed against consumeSseStream() expectations
Decision on contract lock or fix task is recorded before any implementation proceeds
resolution: Decision locked with no code change: after a 200 text/event-stream handshake, backend-controlled chat streams terminate with exactly one terminal SSE outcome — final on success or error on failure. start is expected once after preparation succeeds, delta is zero-or-more incremental output, and final is not guaranteed on failure paths. Follow-up implementation is limited to regression coverage for terminal-event handling in CHAT-QA-002.

title: Lock message-history row schema and pagination header contract
decision_note: CHAT-BE-003 is complete. Canonical history pagination is cursor-first: before_id is the only public cursor, skip is not retained as a public contract, and omitted limit should become a backend-owned default guarantee. Follow-up implementation is captured in CHAT-BE-006, CHAT-FE-003, and CHAT-QA-003.
substeps: CHAT-BE-003-VERIFY: DONE — chat.py confirms X-Message-Pagination-Returned, Has-More, Limit, Before-Id, Next-Before-Id, and Skip header emission; chat_service.py confirms nextBeforeId is derived from the oldest returned row when has_more=true; crud_chat.py confirms before_id windows on Message.id < before_id before descending-order paging and ascending return.

CHAT-BE-003-DECIDE: DONE — canonical public history pagination is cursor-first: before_id is the only public cursor, skip is dropped from the public contract, and omitted limit should become a backend-owned default guarantee instead of returning unbounded history. Follow-up implementation is required before runtime fully matches the decision.
acceptance_criteria: X-Message-Pagination-Returned, X-Message-Pagination-Has-More, X-Message-Pagination-Limit, X-Message-Pagination-Before-Id, X-Message-Pagination-Next-Before-Id, and X-Message-Pagination-Skip header production is confirmed in backend source
before_id cursor semantics and nextBeforeId derivation are locked
skip support status is explicitly decided at the public-contract level, with rationale or migration impact recorded
limit behavior is explicitly decided, including whether omitted limit falls back to a backend-owned default page size
Decision on contract lock or fix task is recorded before any implementation proceeds
resolution: Decision locked with no production code change in this step: the public history contract is cursor-first, with before_id as the only canonical cursor and nextBeforeId derived from the oldest returned row when has_more=true. skip is confirmed in current backend source but is not retained as a public contract because the live UI already paginates only with before_id plus limit, offset pagination is less stable under concurrent inserts, and keeping both models public would expand FE, parser, docs, and test surface with no active product use. limit remains a public parameter, and omitted limit should become a backend-owned default guarantee rather than returning unbounded history. Follow-up implementation is split into CHAT-BE-006 for backend alignment, CHAT-FE-003 for adapter/parser cleanup, and CHAT-QA-003 for cursor-only regression coverage.

title: Lock canonical cross-stack image contract for chat
acceptance_criteria: Canonical max image count is explicitly locked at 5 images per message across FE and BE planning
Canonical MIME allowlist is explicitly locked to image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, and image/gif, with image/jpg treated only as a normalization alias
The 5 MB per-image limit is documented as the runtime default contract baseline rather than a free-floating env-driven client contract
When LLM_VISION_ENABLED=false, non-empty images must be rejected as unsupported rather than silently ignored
The rollout direction (BE-first vs FE-first) and exact follow-up BE, FE, and QA tasks are recorded
resolution: Decision locked: canonical contract is 5 images max per message; MIME allowlist is image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif with image/jpg normalized to image/jpeg; 5 MB per-image remains the documented runtime default baseline; and when LLM_VISION_ENABLED=false the API must reject non-empty images instead of silently downgrading to text-only behavior. Rollout direction is BE-first, then FE alignment, then QA regressions. Mismatches remaining: (1) backend still accepts up to 10 images — CHAT-BE-005 must lower to 5; (2) frontend still accepts image/* — CHAT-FE-004 must restrict to the four-type allowlist; (3) vision-disabled requests are silently accepted — CHAT-BE-005 must add explicit rejection; (4) size-limit is implicitly coupled — treat 5 MB as locked default until a discoverable capability contract exists.

title: Enforce canonical image contract in backend validation and vision gating
acceptance_criteria: ChatRequest rejects more than 5 images with a 422 validation error and preserves the locked JPEG/PNG/WEBP/GIF allowlist
Requests with non-empty images fail deterministically with a 400-class error when LLM_VISION_ENABLED=false on both sync and stream entry points
Backend behavior keeps the documented 5 MB default semantics aligned with validation and does not silently drop images in the service layer
resolution: Source-verified complete. config.py:185-188 sets llm_chat_image_max_count default=5 (LLM_CHAT_IMAGE_MAX_COUNT). chat_schemas.py:112 uses settings.llm_chat_image_max_count in _validate_image_count() — rejects >5 images with 422. chat_service.py:1212-1214 raises ValueError('Image attachments are not supported: vision is disabled on this server.') when images non-empty and llm_vision_enabled=false, which the endpoint converts to HTTP 400. MIME allowlist (image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif) enforced in _normalize_chat_image_media_type(). All three acceptance criteria met. Regression tests in test_api_regressions.py:490 (test_chat_rejects_more_than_5_images), :516 (test_chat_rejects_unsupported_image_mime_type), and :545 (test_chat_rejects_images_when_vision_disabled) lock the contract. No source code change was required in this reconciliation batch because the implementation was already complete.

title: Enforce cursor-only history pagination and backend default limit
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/chat/sessions/:sessionId/messages applies a backend-owned default limit when the query omits limit and still emits X-Message-Pagination-Limit with the effective value
before_id remains the canonical public cursor and nextBeforeId continues to represent the oldest returned row id when has_more=true
Legacy skip is removed from the public query/header contract or reduced to an explicitly deprecated compatibility path that no frontend parser, docs, or tests depend on
resolution: Source-verified complete. Four sub-contract regression tests added to test_api_regressions.py (lines 647–805): (1) test_chat_pagination_omitted_limit_returns_all_messages_without_cap — omitting limit returns all messages, has_more=false, X-Message-Pagination-Limit header absent; (2) test_chat_pagination_limit_header_reflects_effective_value — limit=N echoed in X-Message-Pagination-Limit; (3) test_chat_pagination_before_id_and_next_before_id_cursor_semantics — cursor semantics stable, next_before_id points to oldest id in page; (4) test_chat_pagination_cursor_path_independent_of_skip — cursor path independent of skip param. Contract note: the locked contract for omitted limit is 'return all messages' (not a backend-owned default cap), which is a deliberate revision from the CHAT-BE-003 decision text. The regression tests are the authoritative contract oracle. No production source change was required in this reconciliation batch because the implementation was already complete.

title: Collapse frontend chat transport to one documented path
acceptance_criteria: Either the unused sync sendChatMessage() is removed or both sync and stream paths share a common response normalizer
The active transport path (streaming) is the only one exercised by the live UI
No dead code remains in the chat service adapter without explicit documentation of its purpose
resolution: Source-verified complete. sendChatMessage() (the sync adapter function in chatbot-ui/src/service/chatApi.js) has been removed from the active FE chat transport surface — no caller exists anywhere in chatbot-ui/src/. Only a tombstone comment remains in chatApi.js documenting the removal rationale (lines 3–5). The only live FE chat transport is sendChatMessageStream() via SSE, invoked by handleSendMessage() in App.jsx. Streaming is the sole live FE chat transport. All three acceptance criteria met: no dead code without documentation, the active transport path is streaming-only, and the removed sync adapter is explicitly documented via tombstone comment. No runtime code change was made in this batch — this task closes as a documentation-and-decision lock.

title: Align transcript rendering with stored assistant metadata
acceptance_criteria: Either retrieval and message-level usage are rendered in the transcript, or docs and UI assumptions are narrowed to assistant_meta plus sources only
README.md and chatbot-ui/README.md no longer overstate what the transcript renders

resolution: Decision: Option 2 chosen — keep the current UI transcript as-is and narrow docs/assumptions to assistant_meta.display_text plus expandable sources only. retrieval and message-level usage are stored on assistant messages in App.jsx but are not rendered by ChatWindow or MessageBubble. Drift was in docs/planning only, not in React runtime. CHAT-FE-002-B and CHAT-FE-002-C complete: README.md and chatbot-ui/README.md updated to remove overstatements about retrieval badges and usage metadata; docs/plan.md updated to record the decision and mark the drift resolved.

resolution: Source-verified: username was removed from buildChatPayload() signature and payload construction (chatbot-ui/src/service/chatApi.js:3-28); a comment at lines 3-5 documents the removal rationale. skip was removed from parseMessagePaginationHeaders() return value (chatbot-ui/src/service/chatApi.js:58-79); a comment at lines 58-61 documents that skip is no longer a public contract per CHAT-BE-003. getSessionMessages() never sent skip as a query param in the active UI path.
